title: Intent
description: Work bigger than one Spec: what a person wants, in their words, with its goal, and its slices grouped into phases. A person agrees to it before Specify starts on a slice, and each slice becomes a Spec when its work starts. The team writes it from a brief, the person's raw ask. Aliases: Theme, Program.

id.description: Intent key, such as INTENT-3. An id from before the Intent, such as INIT-1, stays.

title.description: One line. The language in the project's AGENTS.md may apply.

brief.description: The brief it answers, the person's raw ask: a repository path, such as `intent.md`, or a link. aidd never reads or changes it.

status.description: Only a person closes an Intent, because only a person can say its goal is met or dropped: they set `done`, or `cancelled` to stop it. Draft and active are derived from its slices.

agreed_by.description: The person who agreed, in `approved_by`'s form, never an agent. On their yes to `intent.agree`, the agent sets it and `agreed_at` and commits with an `Agreed-by:` trailer. `aidd upgrade` never writes it.

agreed_at.description: When the person agreed (RFC 3339). A slice added or removed, or a new `goal`, after it warns until they agree again.

owner_team.description: The team accountable for the outcome. A slice may name another team in its own `owner_team`.

context.description: Shared terms and constraints for every Spec under this Intent: the one glossary the teams on it share.

trace_id.description: Joins this Intent with the Specs of other repositories that deliver its slices: each sets `trace_id: <home>/<Intent id>`.

reaches.description: How the work reaches users, agreed with the Intent. `incremental` (the default): each Spec merges by itself. `flagged`: each merges behind a flag that stays off until the `launch` Spec. `batched`: the Specs build on one branch, which one Merge approval merges.

launch.description: For `reaches: flagged`: the Spec that turns the feature on for users, planned last. Its Merge approval is the launch, which a person always decides.

covers.description: The ids of the proposal needs this Intent delivers, when it came from an accepted proposal.

proposal.description: The accepted proposal this Intent delivers, so every change under it traces back to what was promised.

go_no_go.description: A person's decision to pursue the Intent or not, in the proposal's shape; `no_go` derives `cancelled`. Never an agent's.

phases.description: The phases, in order, each an ordered group of slices. An Intent with one phase lists `slices` directly instead.

slices.description: The slices of an Intent with one phase, in the order they merge, in place of `phases`.

tracker.description: The tracker's records this Intent links to, such as `{type: epic, id: PORT-31}`. aidd calls no tracker.

risks.description: The R of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

assumptions.description: The A of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

issues.description: The I of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

dependencies.description: The D of the RAID log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here.

decisions.description: The scope decisions log, copied from the accepted proposal and kept current here. Each entry is a person's decision.

allOf.description: An Intent lists its slices in `phases` or, with one phase, in `slices`, never both.
